item.title: FDA OK’s TTFields Device For Pancreatic Cancer
item.description: The FDA approved a wearable tumor-treating fields device (TTFields; Optune Pax) for use with chemotherapy in adults with locally advanced pancreatic cancer.

item.title: Atezo Induction May Up OS in Stage III NSCLC
item.description: New data from the phase 2 APOLO trial showed durable survival and manageable safety with induction atezolizumab before chemoradiation in stage III NSCLC.

item.title: Aakash Desai, MD, MPH, FASCO
item.description: Aakash Desai, MD, MPH, FASCO, is an assistant professor of medicine at the O'Neal Cancer Center, University of Alabama at Birmingham.

item.title: Eric K. Singhi, MD
item.description: Eric K. Singhi, MD, is an assistant professor in the Department of General Oncology and the Division of Cancer Medicine at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston. In his dual appointment, Dr. Singhi is also an assistant professor in the Department of Thoracic/Head and Neck Medical Oncology at MD Anderson’s Division of Cancer Medicine.

item.title: Fawzi Abu Rous, MD
item.description: Fawzi Abu Rous, MD, is a thoracic medical oncologist at Henry Ford Health. Dr. Rous conducts research on lung cancer, specializing in biomarker development. He also leads and designs clinical trials for lung cancer treatment.

item.title: Leah Phillips
item.description: Leah Phillips, a stage IV lung cancer patient and advocate, is the cofounder and executive director of the Young Lung Cancer Initiative, a community to support, uplift, and remember young adults with lung cancer.

item.title: Scott S. Oh, DO
item.description: Scott S. Oh, DO, is professor of clinical medicine, director of the interventional pulmonology quality and outcomes program, and director of the interventional pulmonology fellowship program at the Keck School of Medicine of USC.

item.title: Jessica Donington, MD
item.description: Jessica Donington, MD, is the chief of thoracic surgery at the University of Chicago. She specializes in non-small cell lung cancer.

item.title: Community Oncology Alliance
item.description: Serving as the voice of community oncology in Washington, DC, and across the country, the Community Oncology Alliance (COA) aims to improve patient care, offer professional growth for cancer care providers, and support practice operations.
